Why behaviour changes: Positive health messaging and brand trust reduce perceived risk of tap water and justify higher price, shifting purchase from bottled water to a branded home filter. How value is captured: Aquaporin can capture value through premium pricing, brand loyalty, and repeat purchases of cartridges, leveraging its biomimetic membrane reputation. Assumptions: Consumers currently avoid tap water due to health concerns or taste preference; Aquaporin can communicate health benefits effectively; Price sensitivity is low for premium health products. Predictions: Surveyed health-conscious consumers will express higher intent to purchase a branded home water filter compared to an unbranded alternative; Willingness to pay for a branded filter will be above the price of a comparable unbranded filter; Brand trust will be a significant driver of purchase decisions.

T2: Consumers will adopt a differentiated home water filter if it offers a clear, measurable environmental benefit (e.g., reduced plastic waste), because they are motivated by sustainability and are willing to pay for eco-friendly products. Why behaviour changes: Environmental messaging and proof of impact (e.g., plastic savings) create a perceived benefit that justifies the purchase, shifting behavior from bottled water to a branded home filter. Test "Willingness-to-Pay Survey for Differentiated Consumer Water Purifier" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging and willingness-to-pay (WTP) questions.. Sample: 500 Danish homeowners (ages 25-55) recruited via an online panel, stratified by household income and water purity concerns.. Measure: Average WTP in euros for a branded water purifier marketed as either (a) a health necessity premium product or (b) a convenience/cost-saving subscription service.. Predictions: T1: Higher average WTP for the health-necessity premium product (price above €200) than for the convenience subscription.; T2: Higher average WTP for the convenience subscription service than for the health-necessity premium product.. Decision rule: If the average WTP for the health-necessity premium product exceeds the average WTP for the convenience subscription by at least €50, proceed with developing a differentiated consumer proposition focused on health necessity. If the opposite difference holds, proceed with a convenience-focused proposition. If the difference is within €50, conduct a follow-up survey to resolve ambiguity.. Cost: 15000 euros, 6 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that positions the water purifier as a health-necessity premium product, leveraging Aquaporin's proprietary membrane technology to communicate safety and peace-of-mind benefits. This approach aligns with evidence of consumer perception of tap water as unhealthy and the willingness to pay a premium for branded, high-performance products. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 home espresso enthusiasts considering the same Simonelli single-group machine were assigned equally to two offers. Machine, brand, price, warranty, availability and total contact time were identical. One offer included a structured hands-on home-barista setup lesson; the other included an equal-length product-specification orientation without a skill lesson. There were no discounts. The outcome was a paid, refundable machine reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned enthusiasts per arm. There were 32 reservations in the home-barista-lesson offer arm and 72 in the product-specification-orientation offer arm. This tests the incremental effect of this learning offer among recruited enthusiasts, not a need for a new machine, demand among ordinary coffee drinkers, commercial margins or lasting skill retention. It does not show that every hobby or status mechanism is true or false.

Test "Consumer vs Professional Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with simulated product launch. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two messaging conditions: (A) premium home barista positioning (highlighting social experience, design, and community) or (B) professional shop companion positioning (highlighting integration with existing professional line, service differentiation, and shop-specific features). Both conditions present a compact espresso machine. Sample: 300 participants (150 per condition) recruited via social media and coffee forums, balanced by age, gender, and geographic region. Participants complete a 5-minute survey with purchase intent questions.. Measure: Purchase intent measured on a 7-point scale (1‑ "Would not buy" to 7‑ "Would buy immediately"). Secondary measure: willingness to pay (WTP) in euros.. Predictions: T1: Condition A will achieve a mean purchase intent ≥ 5.5 and mean WTP ≥ €150, indicating sustained premium demand for home barista equipment.; T2: Condition B will achieve a mean purchase intent ≥ 5.5 and mean WTP ≥ €150, indicating demand for professional shop companion equipment.. Decision rule: If condition A’s mean purchase intent ≥ 5.5 AND mean WTP ≥ €150, proceed to develop a differentiated consumer proposition for home barista. If condition B’s mean purchase intent ≥ 5.5 AND mean WTP ≥ €150, develop a companion offering for. Cost: 15000 euros, 10 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition targeting home barista enthusiasts, leveraging premium positioning and community-driven marketing. Begin with a limited launch of a compact espresso machine marketed as a premium home barista tool, using existing Victoria Arduino brand and distribution channels. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

New claim: Home barista culture will sustain demand for premium consumer espresso equipment, allowing Simonelli to capture value through premium pricing and brand positioning.. sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. No study was conducted. Treat this as a what-if only. In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited home cooks considering the same professional-derived combi-steamer were assigned equally to two offers. Both showed identical equipment, brand, cooking specifications, total installed price, warranty, available delivery dates and eventual plumbing/electrical work. One offer bundled an installation coordinator and a site-readiness checklist; the other required the purchaser to arrange the same qualified installers directly. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a discount. All recruited homes were eligible for the stated installation work. The outcome was a paid refundable reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days among all 400 assigned households per arm. There were 32 reservations for the coordinated-installation offer and 72 for the purchaser-arranged offer. This tests whether coordination friction changes choice in that recruited group. It does not show that the appliance fits ordinary kitchens, eliminates drain or power requirements, earns a margin, or justifies diverting resources from professional customers. It does not establish market size or a need for new RATIONAL hardware. A business recommendation can remain unchanged while belief about this narrow coordination mechanism changes.

T1: Home cooks will adopt a differentiated combi-steamer if they perceive it as a premium, professional-grade cooking tool that saves time and delivers consistent results, because they value convenience and quality in their kitchen. Who benefits: Home cooks who cook frequently and want efficient, high-quality cooking solutions.. Why behaviour changes: They shift from traditional cooking methods to a single appliance that combines steaming, boiling, and other functions, reducing the need for multiple devices and simplifying meal preparation.. How value is captured: RATIONAL can charge a premium price for a differentiated product, sell through specialty retailers or online channels, and capture recurring revenue through accessories or subscription services.. Assumptions: Home cooks are willing to pay a premium for a professional-grade cooking system.; The combi-steamer's features (e.g., steam control, temperature precision) are perceived as superior to traditional methods.; Marketing can effectively communicate the professional-grade benefits to home cooks.. Predictions: In a test offering a differentiated combi-steamer at a premium price, purchase intent among home cooks will be higher than for a standard model.; Surveyed home cooks will rank the product higher for convenience and quality compared to a comparable entry-level model..

T2: Home cooks will adopt a differentiated combi-steamer if it is marketed as a subscription-based service that delivers recipes, meal prep guidance, and maintenance, because they seek convenience and personalized cooking support. Who benefits: Home cooks who prefer hands‑off cooking solutions and value ongoing guidance.. Why behaviour changes: They shift from traditional cooking methods to a service that automates meal planning, preparation, and maintenance, reducing the time and effort required to cook.. How value is captured: RATIONAL can monetize through recurring subscription fees, sell premium accessories, and capture data for personalized recommendations, creating a recurring revenue stream.. Assumptions: Home cooks are willing to pay a monthly subscription for cooking support.; The service's content (recipes, guidance) is perceived as valuable and engaging.; The subscription model can be scaled without compromising product quality.. Predictions: In a test offering a subscription‑based combi-steamer, monthly active users will increase over time compared to a product‑only offering.; Surveyed home cooks will indicate higher satisfaction with the service's convenience and personalization than with a standard product..

Test "Home Cook Preference Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized product exposure and willingness-to-pay (WTP) questions.. Sample: 500 home cooks recruited via a panel, balanced for age, gender, and cooking frequency.. Measure: 1) Purchase intent: "Would you buy this differentiated combi-steamer at a premium price?" (binary: Yes/No). 2) WTP premium: "How much more would you pay for this compared to a standard model?" (EUR). 3) Subscription preference: "Would you subscribe to a monthly recipe/service for this combi-steamer?" (binary: Yes/No).. Predictions: T1: Higher purchase intent and higher WTP premium for the differentiated premium model than for a standard model.; T2: Higher subscription preference and higher WTP for the subscription-based model than for the product-only model.. Decision rule: If purchase intent for the differentiated premium model exceeds 40% and its WTP premium exceeds 20% of the standard model's price, proceed with a differentiated premium home-cook proposition. If subscription preference exceeds 40% and WTP for the subscription model exceeds 20% of the premium model's price, pursue a subscription model. If neither condition is met, stay with professional kitchens.. Cost: 18000 euros, 8 weeks.

Favours T1: Develop a differentiated premium home-cook proposition (e.g., compact, smart, or subscription-based combi-steamer) targeting frequent home cooks who value professional-grade convenience and quality. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

T1 kept: The simulated installation-coordination offer test (SYN-RATIONAL-UPDATE) does not address home cook preferences, premium pricing, or subscription models. It tests a narrow coordination mechanism (installation friction) and does not establish market size, hardware need, or value capture for a differentiated combi-steamer. Therefore it does not affect T1. New claim: none. Evidence: SYN-RATIONAL-UPDATE.

Recommendation: Develop a differentiated premium home-cook proposition (e.g., compact, smart, or subscription-based combi-steamer) targeting frequent home cooks who value professional-grade convenience and quality. Target customer: Home cooks who cook frequently and want efficient, high-quality cooking solutions, particularly those who currently use multiple cooking devices.. Value proposition: A premium, professional-grade combi-steamer that combines steaming, boiling, and other functions in a single appliance, offering convenience, consistent results, and potential for recurring revenue through accessories or subscription.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed Home Cook Preference Test (500 respondents, 8 weeks, €18,000) to validate purchase intent and willingness-to-pay for a differentiated premium model versus a standard model.. Uncertainty: The size of the home-cook market, willingness to pay a premium, and the effectiveness of a subscription model remain uncertain. The test will clarify these points before committing resources.. Would change if: If the test shows purchase intent below 40% or WTP premium below 20% of the standard model's price, we would abandon the premium home-cook proposition and stay focused on professional kitchens.; If the test demonstrates strong subscription preference and WTP for a subscription model, we would pursue a subscription-based model.; If new evidence shows home cooks prefer entry-level appliances over premium professional-grade devices, we would reconsider the premium positioning.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Test "Messaging Test: Safety vs Convenience Messaging" between T1; T2. Method: Recruit a sample of 400 adult households (200 per arm) from a panel. Randomly assign participants to one of two message conditions. Arm A receives safety messaging emphasizing membrane technology and water safety. Arm B receives convenience messaging emphasizing low maintenance and easy installation. Both arms present the same Aquaporin-branded water purifier (e.g., ONE) and a generic unbranded alternative. Measure. Sample: 400 adult households (200 per arm), recruited from a panel to ensure diversity in age, income, and water usage habits.. Measure: Primary outcome: purchase intent measured on a 7-point scale (1 = very unlikely, 7 = very likely). Secondary outcome: willingness to pay (WTP) for the branded product in a simulated purchase scenario. Secondary outcome: perceived importance. Predictions: T1: Arm A will show higher purchase intent and WTP than Arm B, because safety messaging aligns with health-conscious consumers who trust membrane technology.; T2: Arm B will show higher purchase intent and WTP than Arm A, because convenience messaging appeals to time-poor households who value low maintenance.. Decision rule: If purchase intent in Arm A is at least 1.5 points higher than Arm B (i.e., ≥5.5 out of 7), conclude T1 is supported and recommend a differentiated safety-focused consumer proposition. If purchase intent in Arm B is at least 1.5 points. Cost: 15000 euros, 10 weeks.

Evidence: SYN-AQP-UPDATE.

Recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that emphasizes membrane technology and water safety, targeting health-conscious households. Use safety messaging in marketing and retail to justify a premium price. Target customer: Health-conscious consumers who prioritize water safety and quality over cost, particularly households with children or those concerned about water quality.. Value proposition: A branded consumer water purifier that leverages Aquaporin's biomimetic membrane technology to provide peace of mind and trust in water safety, positioned as a premium, easy-to-use solution.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed messaging test (400 households, two message conditions) to measure purchase intent and willingness to pay. If safety messaging yields a 1.5-point advantage, proceed to develop a safety-focused consumer line; otherwise,. Uncertainty: The size of the consumer market and willingness to pay a premium for a branded membrane product are uncertain. Would change if: If the messaging test shows convenience messaging outperforms safety messaging by at least 1.5 points, the recommendation would shift to a convenience-focused proposition.; If new public evidence shows strong consumer demand for low-maintenance, time-saving filtration, the case for a differentiated proposition would strengthen.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Test "Premium vs Sustainability Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging condition. Participants view a product description of a differentiated home water purifier (e.g., premium taste and purity) and a description emphasizing sustainability and plastic waste reduction. They then indicate willingness to pay (WTP) on a 7‑point scale and state their top purchase reason.. Sample: 500 adult consumers recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and geographic region to ensure representativeness.. Measure: Willingness to pay (WTP) on a 7‑point scale and top purchase reason (narrative response).. Predictions: T1: Participants exposed to the premium messaging will report higher WTP and will cite taste and purity as their top reason.; T2: Participants exposed to the sustainability messaging will report higher WTP and will cite sustainability as their top reason.. Decision rule: If the average WTP for the premium condition exceeds the average WTP for the sustainability condition by at least 1.5 points (e.g., premium ≥ 5.5 vs sustainability ≥ 4.0), we conclude that the premium positioning drives higher willingness to pay and is more effective. Cost: 20000 euros, 12 weeks.

Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

T1: Home coffee consumers will adopt a differentiated Simonelli consumer proposition if they perceive the product as a visible status signal, because conspicuous consumption increases purchase when income is linked to social status. Who benefits: Simonelli Group gains higher margins and brand prestige by selling premium home machines as status items.. Assumptions: Status-driven consumers are a significant segment of the home coffee market.; Simonelli can effectively communicate status positioning to these consumers.; The current professional brand does not cannibalize the consumer proposition.. T2: Home coffee consumers will adopt a differentiated Simonelli consumer proposition if they perceive the product as a functional, reliable tool for consistent coffee quality, because reliability reduces purchase hesitation and increases repeat purchases. Who benefits: Simonelli Group gains repeat sales and customer loyalty by providing a product that delivers consistent results, increasing overall revenue.. Why behaviour changes: Consumers purchase coffee equipment when they trust the product will perform reliably, reducing the perceived risk of buying a new machine.. How value is captured: Simonelli can price its home machines as reliable, high-quality tools and capture value through repeat purchases and service contracts.. Assumptions: Reliability is a primary purchase driver for home coffee equipment.; Simonelli’s existing professional reputation transfers to consumer positioning.; Consumers are willing to pay a premium for a product they trust to perform consistently.. Test "Status vs Reliability Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online choice-based conjoint survey with simulated purchase decisions. Participants view two home machine descriptions: one emphasizing status (visible, premium, and linked to social status) and one emphasizing reliability (consistent performance, trusted brand). Sample: 400 U.S. adults who report drinking coffee at home, recruited via an online panel. Stratify by income: high-income (>= $80k) vs moderate-income (under $80k).. Measure: Purchase intent (on 7-point scale) and maximum price willingness to pay for each condition.. Predictions: T1: High-income participants will show higher purchase intent and higher willingness to pay when the machine is marketed as a status item.; T2: Moderate-income participants will show higher purchase intent and higher willingness to pay when the machine is marketed on reliability.. Decision rule: If the average purchase intent in the status condition is at least 1.5 points higher than the average intent in the reliability condition among high-income participants, proceed with a status-positioned consumer proposition. If the difference is less than 1.5 points, proceed with a reliability-positioned proposition. If both conditions show similar intent differences, do not expand into a consumer proposition.. Cost: 18000 euros, 8 weeks.

Test "Dual‑message survey and pilot test" between T1; T2. Method: Run a targeted online survey with two parallel paths. Path A presents a convenience‑focused message emphasizing time savings, health benefits, and a single appliance that replaces multiple tools. Path B presents a space‑saving message emphasizing reduced clutter, consistent results, and a single high‑performance device. Participants in both paths are shown a mock combi‑steamer description and asked to indicate maximum price they would pay and likelihood to purchase.. Sample: 400 German adults recruited via an online panel, stratified by age and household income to reflect typical home‑cook demographics.. Measure: 1) Maximum price willing to pay (EUR). 2) Purchase intent (binary: would buy). 3) Primary purchase driver (open‑ended).. Predictions: T1: Path A will achieve a higher average maximum price and higher purchase intent than Path B, and at least 60% of respondents will cite convenience, health benefits, or time savings as their top driver.; T2: Path B will achieve a higher average maximum price and higher purchase intent than Path A, and at least 60% of respondents will cite space savings, clutter reduction, or consistent results as their top driver.. Decision rule: If the average maximum price and purchase intent for Path A exceed Path B by at least 10% and the primary driver for Path A is convenience, health, or time savings, proceed with a differentiated home‑cook proposition. If Path B exceeds Path A by at least 10% and the primary driver is space savings, maintain focus on professional kitchens. If neither path meets its threshold, do not expand into consumer markets.. Cost: 18000 euros, 10 weeks.

Favours T1: Develop a differentiated home‑cook proposition built on the existing combi‑steamer technology, targeting convenience‑driven home cooks with a single, high‑performance appliance that combines steaming, boiling, and other cooking functions. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Recommendation: Develop a differentiated home‑cook proposition built on the existing combi‑steamer technology, targeting convenience‑driven home cooks with a single, high‑performance appliance that combines steaming, boiling, and other cooking functions. Target customer: Home cooks who value convenience, health benefits, and time savings, and have limited kitchen space.. Value proposition: A single, high‑performance combi‑steamer that reduces prep time, offers versatile cooking functions, and positions RATIONAL as a convenient, health‑focused cooking solution.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed dual‑message survey and pilot test (400 German adults, two paths) to validate willingness to pay and purchase intent. Use the decision rule: if Path A exceeds Path B by at least 10% and convenience is the top driver, move. Uncertainty: The size of the home‑cook market and their willingness to pay a premium for a combi‑steamer are unknown. Evidence shows RATIONAL already serves professional kitchens and has a strong commercial focus, but no public source shows consumer. Would change if: If the survey shows Path B (space‑saving) exceeds Path A by at least 10% and space savings are the top driver, we would maintain focus on professional kitchens and not develop a consumer proposition.; If a new source shows RATIONAL already sells a consumer line or has a significant home‑cook market, we would reconsider the recommendation.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. No study was conducted. Treat this as a what-if only. In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited home cooks considering the same professional-derived combi-steamer were assigned equally to two offers. Both showed identical equipment, brand, cooking specifications, total installed price, warranty, available delivery dates and eventual plumbing/electrical work. One offer bundled an installation coordinator and a site-readiness checklist; the other required the purchaser to arrange the same qualified installers directly. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a discount. All recruited homes were eligible for the stated installation work. The outcome was a paid refundable reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days among all 400 assigned households per arm. There were 32 reservations for the coordinated-installation offer and 72 for the purchaser-arranged offer. This tests whether coordination friction changes choice in that recruited group. It does not show that the appliance fits ordinary kitchens, eliminates drain or power requirements, earns a margin, or justifies diverting resources from professional customers. It does not establish market size or a need for new RATIONAL hardware. A business recommendation can remain unchanged while belief about this narrow coordination mechanism changes.

Test "Consumer Preference Test: Premium vs. Sustainable Combi-Steamer" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with two randomized arms: Arm A (premium positioning) offers a consumer combi-steamer priced at €1,200 with emphasis on convenience and quality; Arm B (sustainable positioning) offers the same appliance priced at €1,200 with emphasis on energy efficiency and environmental impact. Participants are randomly assigned to one arm, and then asked about purchase intent (1‑10 scale) and willingness to pay a premium over a comparable existing appliance.. Sample: 500 German adult home cooks recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and household income to ensure representativeness.. Measure: Purchase intent score (1‑10) and willingness to pay a premium (EUR) for the consumer combi-steamer.. Predictions: T1: Higher purchase intent and willingness to pay a premium in Arm A (premium positioning) compared to Arm B.; T2: Higher purchase intent and willingness to pay a premium in Arm B (sustainable positioning) compared to Arm A.. Decision rule: If the difference in purchase intent between Arm A and Arm B is at least 5 points (e.g., Arm A – 6.5 vs. Arm B – 1.5), conclude the premium positioning (T1) is more effective. If the difference is at least 5 points in favor of sustainability (Arm B – 6.5 vs. Arm A – 1.5), conclude the sustainable positioning (T2) is more effective. If neither difference meets the threshold, the test is inconclusive and further research is needed.. Cost: 18000 euros, 8 weeks.

In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 households already using a compatible drinking-water purifier received the same membrane specifications, water-quality information, brand, warranty and total annual price. Half were offered a prepaid plan with scheduled cartridge delivery and replacement reminders; half were offered a prepaid self-service cartridge plan without that delivery schedule or reminders. There were no discounts. The outcome was a paid plan enrollment remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned households per arm. This what-if assumes an authorised operator can legally supply and service the offer; it does not change the dossier evidence about Aquaporin's insolvency or financing. There were 120 plan enrollments in the scheduled-delivery-and-reminder plan arm and 60 in the self-service cartridge plan arm. This tests willingness to enroll in a maintenance offer under that conditional supply assumption, not membrane efficacy, correct long-term filter use, market size, company solvency or Aquaporin's ability to fund an offer. An unchanged business recommendation can be justified by those other constraints.

events.text: Objective: Determine whether there is sufficient public evidence to justify Aquaporin A/S investing in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case beyond its current water-membrane offering.. Constraints: Limited to public sources; no internal company data available; Search budget of 8 searches; Test budget of €20,000 and 12-week timeframe for any proposed experiment; Must identify evidence of consumer demand, willingness to pay, and competitive landscape. Alternatives: Develop a differentiated consumer proposition targeting a specific use case (e.g., home water filtration for a particular segment); Expand the existing water-membrane offering to new markets or applications without a differentiated consumer proposition; Maintain current business model and not pursue any new consumer proposition; Partner with or license the technology to consumer brands rather than selling directly to consumers.

T1: Consumers will adopt a differentiated consumer proposition if they perceive the water source as unsafe or unhealthy, leading them to choose a branded home water filter that promises purity. Who benefits: Consumers seeking safe drinking water and brands that can communicate purity claims.. Why behaviour changes: Negative perceptions of tap water (e.g., contamination, taste) create a willingness to pay for a branded solution that promises safety.. How value is captured: Aquaporin can charge a premium for a branded purifier and capture value through direct-to-consumer sales and brand loyalty.. Assumptions: Consumers trust brand claims about water purity.; Negative perceptions of tap water are widespread enough to drive purchase.; Aquaporin can effectively communicate purity claims to consumers.. Predictions: In markets with high bottled-water consumption, consumers will show higher purchase intent for a branded home water filter compared to an unbranded alternative.; Willingness to pay for a branded purifier will be above the price of a generic membrane unit.; Brand awareness of Aquaporin will correlate with purchase intent..

T2: Consumers will adopt a differentiated consumer proposition if they perceive the water source as safe and reliable, leading them to choose a branded home water filter that emphasizes purity and trust. Who benefits: Consumers who prioritize water safety and reliability, and brands that can communicate trust in their water supply.. Why behaviour changes: Positive perceptions of tap water safety and reliability reduce uncertainty about water quality, making consumers more willing to invest in a branded purifier.. How value is captured: Aquaporin can charge a premium for a branded purifier and capture value through direct-to-consumer sales and brand positioning as a trusted water provider.. Assumptions: Consumers trust brand claims about water purity and safety.; Positive perceptions of tap water are widespread enough to drive purchase.; Aquaporin can effectively communicate safety and purity claims to consumers.. Predictions: In markets where tap water quality is perceived as high, consumers will show higher purchase intent for a branded home water filter compared to an unbranded alternative.; Willingness to pay for a branded purifier will be above the price of a generic membrane unit.; Brand awareness of Aquaporin will correlate with purchase intent in safety-focused markets..

Does not show: It does not show that these negative perceptions translate into actual purchase of a branded home water filter, nor does it address Aquaporin's ability to communicate purity claims..

Test "Consumer Messaging Test: Safety vs. Safety and Reliability" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey experiment with randomized messaging conditions.. Sample: 500 adult consumers in a safety-focused market (e.g., Europe) screened for current water filter ownership.. Measure: Purchase intent (binary: would buy a branded home water filter) and willingness to pay (WTP) on a 7-point scale.. Predictions: T1: Safety-focused condition will generate higher purchase intent and WTP than the safety-reliability condition.; T2: Safety-reliability condition will generate higher purchase intent and WTP than the safety-focused condition.. Decision rule: If the safety-reliability condition achieves a purchase intent rate at least 10 percentage points higher than the safety-focused condition AND a WTP difference of at least DKK 50 (or equivalent), proceed to develop a differentiated consumer. Cost: 18000 euros, 6 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that emphasizes water safety and purity, particularly in markets where tap water is perceived as unsafe or unhealthy. Begin with a targeted pilot to test purchase intent and willingness to pay before scaling. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

T1 kept: The simulated maintenance-convenience proposition test (SYN-AQP-UPDATE) does not address consumer perceptions of tap water safety or willingness to pay for a branded purifier. It tests willingness to enroll in a maintenance offer under a conditional supply assumption, which does not provide evidence for or against T1. New claim: none. Evidence: SYN-AQP-UPDATE.

Recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that emphasizes water safety and purity, particularly in markets where tap water is perceived as unsafe or unhealthy. Begin with a targeted pilot to test purchase intent and willingness to pay before scaling. Target customer: Consumers in regions where tap water quality is uncertain or perceived as unsafe, such as areas with high bottled-water consumption or where water safety concerns are prominent.. Value proposition: A branded home water purifier that promises purity and safety, leveraging Aquaporin's membrane technology to address consumer concerns about water quality.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed Consumer Messaging Test (online survey with safety-focused vs. safety-reliability messaging) to validate purchase intent and willingness to pay before committing to a full-scale launch.. Uncertainty: The extent to which consumers will actually purchase a branded purifier based on safety perceptions remains uncertain; the test will provide critical data to resolve this.. Would change if: If the pilot shows purchase intent below a threshold (e.g., <10%) or willingness to pay significantly below the price of a generic membrane unit, the investment would be reconsidered in favor of a different strategy.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.
